title: COVID-19 Lockdowns Produce UK's Deepest Recession in Three Centuries
reason: Confirmed via ONS (official UK statistics agency) and multiple independent news outlets. ONS's first quarterly estimate bulletin for April-June 2020 confirms UK GDP fell a record 20.4% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 2020, the largest decline since quarterly records began in 1955, following a Q1 2020 decline (reported across ONS revision vintages as -2.2% to -3.0%, consistent with the event's "2.6%" figure being one such vintage). CNBC/CNN (Feb 2021) independently confirm full-year 2020 GDP contracted 9.9%, the worst annual UK slump since the Great Frost of 1709 (per Bank of England historical database), exceeding even the 1921 post-WWI slump — matching the "deepest recession in three centuries" framing, which itself is directly corroborated by a Resolution Foundation press release title using that exact phrase. Q3 2020 rebound is confirmed in ONS/CNBC sources at 15.5% (preliminary)/16.1% (revised) — in the same ballpark as the event's cited 17.6%, plausibly a later revision vintage; this is a normal data-vintage variance, not a substantive discrepancy. The core claims (magnitude, timing, causation via lockdowns, twice the 2008-09 decline, historic severity) are all solidly corroborated by ONS plus independent press (CNBC, CNN, Resolution Foundation).
